items.text: The wake word engine's extractFeatures() and compareBest() are stateless pure functions — live testing can call them directly without instantiating a PassiveListener. This keeps the implementation simple and avoids any interaction with the detection pipeline.

acceptance_allow could not be auto-set — the backlog update API returned 405. Intended globs: scenarios/web-console/ui/src/components/settings/VoiceInputSection.tsx, scenarios/web-console/ui/src/hooks/voice/**, scenarios/web-console/api/** (though backend changes are unlikely).

items.topic: Audio capture approach for live testing
items.context: The test UI needs to continuously capture speech segments and run them through the engine. There are two main approaches: reuse the PassiveListener's VAD+ring-buffer pipeline (heavyweight, full detection loop) or build a lightweight capture loop directly in the component using MediaRecorder + decodeAudioData (same pattern already used for enrollment recording).

options.label: Lightweight MediaRecorder loop in component
options.rationale: Reuses the same recording pattern from enrollment (MediaRecorder → Blob → decodeAudioData → extractFeatures). Simple to implement, no coupling to PassiveListener. Each test attempt is a discrete recording. User clicks 'Test' or holds a button, audio is captured, features extracted, and compared. Recommended because it's the simplest approach that works and avoids modifying detection internals.

options.label: Reuse PassiveListener in test mode
options.rationale: Instantiate PassiveListener with a test callback that reports scores instead of triggering voice input. Gets VAD-based automatic speech detection for free. But couples test UI to PassiveListener internals, and PassiveListener wasn't designed for score reporting — would need changes (violates non-goal of not modifying detection pipeline).

options.label: Continuous AudioWorklet with VAD
options.rationale: Use AudioWorklet for real-time audio processing with VAD to automatically detect speech segments and compare. Most responsive UX but significantly more complex to implement, and MFCC extraction would need to run in the worklet thread or be posted back to main thread.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.context: How should the user trigger each test attempt? This affects UX complexity and how natural the testing flow feels.

options.label: Push-to-test button (hold to record, release to compare)
options.rationale: User holds a button, speaks the wake word, releases. System extracts features and shows result. Simple, explicit, no VAD needed. Each attempt is clearly delineated. Recommended for simplicity and because it mirrors the enrollment recording UX the user already knows.

options.label: Continuous listening mode (start/stop toggle with auto-detection)
options.rationale: User clicks 'Start Testing', system continuously listens using VAD to detect speech segments automatically, compares each one, and shows results in a stream. More like real passive-listening behavior but requires VAD integration and is harder to implement correctly.

options.label: Tap-to-record (tap starts, tap again or auto-stop ends)
options.rationale: Single tap starts recording, auto-stops after silence or max duration (like enrollment). Simpler than hold-to-talk but less explicit about when to speak.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.context: After each test attempt, the user needs to see whether it matched and how close the score was to the threshold. This helps with threshold tuning.

options.label: Score bar with threshold line
options.rationale: Horizontal bar showing the match score (0-1) with a vertical line at the threshold position. Bar is green above threshold, red below. Intuitive and compact. Recommended because it gives both the absolute score and threshold relationship at a glance.

options.label: Numeric score with pass/fail badge
options.rationale: Show the raw score number (e.g., '0.72') next to a green checkmark or red X. Simple and minimal but harder to understand threshold relationship.

options.label: Score bar + numeric + history chart
options.rationale: Combines the bar visualization with a numeric readout and a mini chart showing score history over multiple attempts. Most informative but adds significant UI complexity for a settings-page feature.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.context: Should the UI keep a history of test attempts so the user can see patterns across multiple tries?

options.label: Scrollable list of last 10 attempts
options.rationale: Each entry shows: score bar, pass/fail, timestamp. Lets the user see consistency across attempts and tune threshold accordingly. Recommended because it provides meaningful feedback without overcomplicating the UI.

options.label: Single latest result only
options.rationale: Only show the most recent test result. Simplest possible UI. User has to remember prior scores mentally. May be sufficient for a first iteration.

options.label: No history — just live feedback during active test
options.rationale: Show result only while testing is active, clear it when done. Minimal state management but poor UX for threshold tuning.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.context: How should we verify that the live test feature works correctly? The core engine already has unit tests (dtw.test.ts, mfcc.test.ts, wakeWordEngine.test.ts). The new code is primarily UI wiring.

options.label: Manual testing only for this UI feature
options.rationale: The feature is a thin UI layer over already-tested engine functions. The interesting behavior (mic capture → feature extraction → comparison) requires real browser APIs that are hard to mock meaningfully. Manual testing with actual speech is the most reliable verification. Recommended for pragmatism.

options.label: Unit tests for the test-loop hook/logic
options.rationale: Extract the test logic into a custom hook and unit test the state machine (idle → recording → comparing → result). Mock the engine calls. Catches state management bugs but doesn't verify the actual audio pipeline.

options.label: E2E test with synthetic audio
options.rationale: Use Playwright to inject synthetic audio into the mic and verify the UI shows match/reject. Most thorough but very complex setup and brittle.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach
